# Pandamonium v1.0.71

Marketplace discovery now recovers legacy installations that were unintentionally frozen on an old bundled catalog. The release preserves custom channels and installed-plugin state. Rollback is signed v1.0.70 with the updater snapshot.

## MAD-970 — Marketplace: restore public catalog parity on legacy installations

### Problem

Older installations can retain Pandamonium's bundled public trust store as a local `trusted_keys.json`. The shared loader treated every local trust file as an operator-managed channel, so those installations never refreshed the signed public catalog. CT103 consequently showed only Oracle while a fresh installation saw the current catalog, including PandaFlix and ani-cli.

### Implementation

The shared marketplace loader now compares local trust data with the bundled public trust set. An equivalent copy is treated as legacy public cache state and follows the existing bounded signed refresh path. A different trust set remains operator-managed and returns its locally signed catalog without a network refresh. No trust file, catalog signature rule, install path or registry format changed.

### Product value and UI visibility

Marketplace shows the same signed public package catalog on upgraded and fresh installations. Installed remains installation-owner state; this release neither installs nor removes plugins. The refreshed catalog makes PandaFlix and ani-cli discoverable before the Entertainment player integration lands.

### Verification

A focused regression proves both paths: bundled-equivalent legacy trust refreshes, while a distinct valid custom channel remains local. The relevant marketplace suite passed 36 checks locally. Protected CI passed the full Python suite, Chromium browser suite, syntax, secret, workflow and container gates. CT103 catalog and installed-registry readback are completed through the protected updater after publication.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency, environment variable, schema, permission or database change. Existing custom trust stores remain authoritative. The public channel still uses its fixed repository, branch, signature validation, refresh throttle and last-known-good fallback. This release fixes discovery parity only; the native Entertainment UI and playback controls are separate follow-up work.
